words: فإن لم تجدوا فيها أحدا فلا تدخلوها حتى يؤذن لكم
rows.speaker: القمي
rows.claim: Al-Qummi explains that if no one is present to grant permission, one must not enter until permission is given.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير القمي في قوله تعالى { فإن لم تجدوا فيها أحدا فلا تدخلوها

words: بيوتا غير مسكونة فيها متاع لكم
rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Al-Qummi reports from al-Sadiq that baths, inns, and mills count as uninhabited houses with useful property and may be entered without permission.
rows.anchor: قال الصادق عليه السلام هي الحمامات والخانات والأرحية تدخلها بغير إذن

words: قل للمؤمنين يغضوا من أبصارهم ويحفظوا فروجهم
rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Al-Zubayri's report from al-Sadiq treats the eye's duty to avoid forbidden sights and turn from what is unlawful as a bodily obligation and part of faith.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عمرو الزبيري عن أبي عبد الله عليه اللسلام في حديث

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: The report explains lowering the gaze and guarding private parts as forbidding men and women to look at one another's nakedness and to expose their own.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عبد الله عليه اللسلام في حديث يذكر فيه ما فرض الله على الجوارح

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq says that guarding the private parts means avoiding fornication throughout the Qur'an, except in these verses, where it means guarding them from being looked at.
rows.anchor: وقال كل شيء في القرآن من حفظ الفرج فهو من الزنا إلا هذه الآية فهو من النظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabatabai notes that al-Qummi transmits the report through his father, Ibn Abi Umayr, and Abu Basir from the Imam; similar reports are attributed to Abu al-Aliya and Ibn Zayd.
rows.anchor: وروي مثله عن أبي العالية وابن زيد

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: An Anṣari youth followed a passing woman with his gaze, injured his face on a projecting object, then told the Prophet; Gabriel then brought the command to lower the gaze.
rows.anchor: وفي الكافي بإسناده عن سعد الإسكاف عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال استقبل شاب

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Al-Durr al-manthur transmits a parallel account of the injured youth from Ibn Mardawayh, tracing it to Ali ibn Abi Talib.
rows.anchor: ورواه في الدر المنثور عن ابن مردويه عن علي بن أبي طالب مثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabatabai reads the report's apparent command as prohibiting any gaze at a non-mahram woman, while some earlier reports appear to limit the prohibition to another person's private parts.
rows.anchor: وظاهر الحديث أن المراد بالأمر بالغض في الآية النهي عن مطلق النظر إلى الأجنبية

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: A report from al-Sadiq permits a man to see a non-mahram woman's face, hands, and feet.
rows.anchor: وفيه بإسناده عن مروك بن عبيد عن بعض أصحابنا عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Al-Khisal gives the permitted visible parts as the face, hands, and feet, in a wording parallel to the preceding report.
rows.anchor: ورواه في الخصال عن بعض أصحابنا عنه عليه السلام ولفظه الوجه والكفين والقدمين

rows.speaker: موسى بن جعفر
rows.claim: Musa al-Kazim answers that a man may see a non-lawful woman's face, hand, and the place of her bracelet.
rows.anchor: وفي قرب الأسناد للحميري عن علي بن جعفر عن أخيه موسى بن جعفر عليه السلام

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq permits looking at the heads of women from Tihama, Bedouins, the Sawad, and non-Arabs because they do not heed prohibitions, and at mentally incapacitated women; their hair and bodies may be viewed without deliberately seeking it.
rows.anchor: وفي الكافي بإسناده عن عباد بن صهيب قال سمعت أبا عبد الله عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabatabai glosses the report's restriction against deliberate looking as avoidance of looking with suspicion or desire.
rows.anchor: أقول كأنه عليه السلام يريد بقوله ما لم يتعمد ذلك، الريبة

rows.speaker: محمد
rows.claim: The Prophet told Ali that the first glance is allowed to him, while a second glance counts against him.
rows.anchor: وفي الخصال وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم لأمير المؤمنين عليه السلام

rows.speaker: محمد
rows.claim: A parallel report from Burayda says not to follow one glance with another: the first is allowed, the later one is not.
rows.anchor: وروى مثله في الدر المنثور عن عدة من أصحاب الجوامع عن بريدة عنه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: أم سلمة
rows.claim: After the hijab command, the Prophet told Umm Salama and Maymuna to veil from Ibn Umm Maktum; when they objected that he was blind, he asked whether they too were blind and unable to see him.
rows.anchor: وفي جوامع الجامع عن أم سلمة قالت

rows.speaker: أم سلمة
rows.claim: Al-Durr al-manthur also transmits Umm Salama's report through Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, and al-Bayhaqi.
rows.anchor: ورواه في الدر المنثور عن أبي داود والترمذي والنسائي والبيهقي عنها

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq says a woman should not uncover before a Jewish or Christian woman, since such women might describe her to their husbands.
rows.anchor: وفي الفقيه وروى حفص بن البختري عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: A view, transmitted from al-Sadiq, takes those whose right hands are possessed to mean male and female slaves.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه العبيد والإماء وروي ذلك عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq identifies men without sexual desire as fools under another's control who do not approach women.
rows.anchor: وفي الكافي بإسناده عن عبد الرحمن بن أبي عبد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage gathers traits matching the disbelievers' objections: mocking the Messenger, following desire, worshipping what cannot harm or benefit, and refusing to prostrate to God.
rows.anchor: مما يناسب سنخ اعتراضاتهم واقتراحاتهم كاستهزائهم الرسول صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural pronoun refers to the previously mentioned disbelievers; when they see the Prophet, they treat him only as an object of mockery.
rows.anchor: ضمير الجمع للذين كفروا السابق ذكرهم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Huzʾ means mockery or derision, and here the verbal noun denotes the person being mocked.
rows.anchor: والهزؤ الاستهزاء والسخرية فالمصدر بمعنى المفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their question, “Is this the one God sent as a messenger?”, spells out what their mockery sounds like.
rows.anchor: وقوله { أهذا الذي بعث الله رسولا } بيان لاستهزائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “in kāda,” inna is the reduced form of the emphatic particle; iḍlāl carries the sense of turning someone aside, which explains its construction with ʿan.
rows.anchor: من الثقيلة، والإضلال كأنه مضمن معنى الصرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answer to lawlā is omitted but supplied by the preceding clause: without holding firm to worshipping their gods, they would have been diverted from them.
rows.anchor: وجواب لولا محذوف يدل عليه ما تقدمه، والمعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God threatens them and warns that, when they witness the punishment, they will know with certainty their error and deviation.
rows.anchor: توعد وتهديد منه تعالى لهم وتنبيه أنهم على غفلة مما سيستقبلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hawā is the soul's inclination toward desire when reason does not moderate it.
rows.anchor: الهوى ميل النفس إلى الشهوة من غير تعديله بالعقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking desire as a god means obeying and following it instead of God; the Qur'an often condemns following desire and calls obedience to another being worship.
rows.anchor: والمراد باتخاذ الهوى إلها طاعته واتباعه من دون الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is a rebuke that denies the Prophet is responsible for managing or guiding this person to right conduct; he cannot do so after God has let him stray and cut off guidance.
rows.anchor: استفهام إنكاري أي لست أنت وكيلا عليه قائما على نفسه وباموره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their rejection is persistent rejection of every reminder that comes to them, not rejection of a new reminder while accepting an old one; naming the Merciful points to revelation as an expression of universal mercy for worldly and afterlife welfare.
rows.anchor: في ذكر صفة الرحمن إشارة إلى أن الذكر الذي يأتيهم إنما ينشأ عن صفة الرحمة العامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their denial follows from their continued turning away from every reminder; the news of what they mocked means the near and later punishments that will befall them.
rows.anchor: تفريع على ما تقدم من استمرار إعراضهم، وقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question rebukes them; its clause is conjoined to an implied reminder that they persist in turning away and have failed to look at God's plants.
rows.anchor: الاستفهام للإنكار التوبيخي والجملة معطوف على مقدر يدل عليه المقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb for seeing includes the sense of looking here, which accounts for its construction with ilā.
rows.anchor: فالرؤية في قوله { أو لم يروا } مضمنة معنى النظر ولذا عديت بإلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent referent of the noble pair is a beautiful plant kind; God created plant kinds in pairs.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد بالزوج الكريم. وهو الحسن

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes the noble pair to include animals, especially human beings, citing God's statement that He grew you from the earth like plants.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بالزوج الكريم الذي أنبته الله يعم الحيوان وخاصة الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Planting every noble pair is a sign because God creates each pair, completes each one's deficiencies through its mate, directs both to their intended ends, and guides each toward final happiness; a God acting this way will guide humanity too.
rows.anchor: حيث أن فيه إيجادا لكل زوج منه وتتميم نقائص كل من الزوجين بالآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Given their settled habit of turning away and their failed capacity to receive guidance, it was not expected that most of them would believe.
rows.anchor: لم يكن المترقب من حال أكثرهم بما عندهم من ملكة الاعراض وبطلان الاستعداد أن يؤمنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence of earlier prophets shows that Muhammad's people follow the same path and will face punishment; repeated story endings echo the opening rejection, console the Prophet, show his mission is not unprecedented, and implicitly warn his people.
rows.anchor: ليظهر أن قوم النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم سائرون مسيرهم وسيردون موردهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse asks the Prophet to recall when God called Moses and sent him to Pharaoh's people to rescue the Children of Israel, as detailed in Surat Taha and elsewhere.
rows.anchor: أي واذكر وقتا نادى فيه ربك موسى وبعثه بالرسالة إلى قوم فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command explains the call; describing them first as wrongdoers and then as Pharaoh's people points to their shirk and their abuse of the Israelites as the reason for the mission.
rows.anchor: وتوصيفهم أولا بالظالمين ثم بيانه ثانيا بقوم فرعون للإشارة إلى حكمة الإرسال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The third-person wording is a rebuke delivered from afar; in the commissioning context it means Moses should tell them that his Lord reproaches their abandonment of piety.
rows.anchor: بصيغة الغيبة، وهو توبيخ غيابي منه تعالى لهم

rows.speaker: مجمع البيان
rows.claim: Majmaʿ al-Bayan defines fear as the soul's disturbance from anticipating harm, opposite to security as the soul's calm in expectation of unalloyed benefit.
rows.anchor: قال في مجمع البيان الخوف انزعاج النفس بتوقع الضر ونقيضه الأمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabatabai distinguishes fear, usually an apprehension that prompts practical precaution even without inner agitation, from khashya, the soul's disturbed anxiety at expected harm; this explains why God denies prophets fear of others but sometimes affirms ordinary fear.
rows.anchor: وأكثر ما يطلق الخوف على إحساس الشر بحيث يؤدي إلى الإتقاء عملا وإن لم تضطرب النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the stories of Moses and Abraham, the account turns to Noah, the first of the foremost prophets; most of his people disbelieved, so God drowned them and saved Noah and the believers with him.
rows.anchor: وهو أول أولي العزم سادة الأنبياء

rows.speaker: المفردات
rows.claim: Al-Mufradat says qawm originally denotes a group of men, not women, citing the verse about one people not mocking another and a poet's contrast between men and women.
rows.anchor: قال في المفردات القوم جماعة الرجال في الأصل دون النساء

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The cited line “Are the people of Al-Hisn men or women?” uses qawm to mean a group of men.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر أقوم آل حصن أم نساء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One grammatical analysis treats qawm as masculine and explains a feminine predicate by taking the word to mean a collective group.
rows.anchor: ولفظ القوم قيل مذكر وتأنيث الفعل المسند إليه بتأويل الجماعة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A second analysis treats qawm itself as feminine.
rows.anchor: وقيل مؤنث وقال في المصباح يذكر ويؤنث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although qawm originally names men, in most Qur'anic usage it denotes both men and women.
rows.anchor: وفي عامة القرآن أريدوا به والنساء جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah's people are called deniers of all messengers because their call to monotheism was one unified message, so rejecting Noah amounted to rejecting them all; God likewise counts belief in some messengers but not others as disbelief in all.
rows.anchor: إنما هو من جهة أن دعوتهم واحدة وكلمتهم متفقة على التوحيد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation takes the plural generically, like saying someone rides mounts and wears cloaks though he has only one of each; al-Tabatabai prefers the unified-message explanation, and the same alternatives apply to the accounts of ʿAd and Thamud.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو من قبيل قولهم فلان يركب الدواب ويلبس البرود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Their brother” means a kinsman, as in expressions such as a brother of Tamim or Kalb; the question is reproachful.
rows.anchor: المراد بالأخ النسيب كقولهم أخو تميم واخو كليب والاستفهام للتوبيخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah is a trustworthy messenger who conveys only what God commanded; therefore he tells them to fear God and obey him, since obedience to the messenger is obedience to God.
rows.anchor: أي رسول من الله سبحانه أمين على ما حملته من الرسالة لا أبلغكم إلا ما أمرني ربي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By asking no worldly wage, Noah shows he seeks their good without betrayal or deception; the renewed call to fear and obey follows because each of his trustworthiness and lack of payment independently obliges them to obey.
rows.anchor: مسوق لنفي الطمع الدنيوي بنفي سؤال الأجر فيثبت بذلك أنه ناصح لهم

words: إِنْ أَجْرِىَ إِلَّا عَلَىٰ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God “Lord of the worlds” rather than simply “God” makes monotheism explicit: the people regarded God as a high god while assigning other gods to other worlds, and this wording denies all rival gods.
rows.anchor: للدلالة على صريح التوحيد فإنهم كانوا يرون أنه تعالى إله عالم الآلهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ardhalun is the regular plural of ardhal, a superlative from baseness; Noah's opponents mean people with lowly conduct and menial pursuits.
rows.anchor: الأرذلون جمع أرذل على الصحة وهو اسم تفضيل من الرذالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They likely measure honor by wealth, sons, and followers, and call slaves, the poor, and low-status artisans lowly because elites avoid their company.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنهم كانوا يرون الشرف والكرامة في الأموال والجموع من البنين والاتباع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun is Noah's; ma is interrogative, though some take it as a negation with an omitted predicate recoverable from context.
rows.anchor: استفهامية وقيل نافية وعليه فالخبر محذوف لدلالة السياق عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Either grammatical analysis means Noah denies knowing what they did before believing in him, as the past-tense wording indicates.
rows.anchor: والمراد على اي حال نفي علمه بأعمالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “My Lord” here means the Lord of the worlds, the God Noah uniquely called them to worship.
rows.anchor: رب العالمين فإنه الذي كان يختص نوح بالدعوة إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is syntactically cut off from the preceding construction and means “if you had any sense”; the alternative that it means they would then understand something is dismissed.
rows.anchor: مقطوع عن العمل أي لو كان لكم شعور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah says he neither knows their previous deeds nor has responsibility to investigate and judge them; his Lord will account for them and repay them according to their deeds.
rows.anchor: وإنما حسابهم على ربي { لو تشعرون } فيجازيهم حسب أعمالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that Noah is only a clear warner explains why he will not expel believers or investigate their past to judge them: accounting belongs to God, not him.
rows.anchor: الآية الثانية بمنزلة التعليل للأولى والمجموع متمم للبيان السابق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their demand that Noah desist means that he stop preaching; rujm means stoning, and this threat marks the last stage of their dealings with him.
rows.anchor: المراد بالانتهاء ترك الدعوة، والرجم هو الرمي بالحجارة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A view takes rujm figuratively as verbal abuse, but al-Tabatabai calls that interpretation remote.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد به الشتم وهو بعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat is phrased as a firm, emphatic assertion, matching the final and forceful character of their warning.
rows.anchor: يهددونه عليه السلام بقول جازم كما يشهد به ما في الكلام من وجوه التأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah's prayer seeks a decisive judgment; he first states that his people have wholly rejected him as a prelude, since the established denial leaves no prospect that they will believe.
rows.anchor: هذا استفتاح منه عليه السلام وقد قدم له قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story concerns Hud and ʿAd; as in Noah's story, the people are called deniers of the messengers although they outwardly rejected only one.
rows.anchor: بيان تشير الآيات إلى قصة هود عليه السلام وقومه وهم قوم عاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAd were an early Arab people who lived in al-Ahqaf, had settled dwellings, fertile land, and an advanced civilization, but rejected messengers, spurned blessings, and rebelled; a barren wind destroyed their homes and erased their traces.
rows.anchor: كانوا يسكنون الأحقاف من جزيرة العرب لهم مدنية راقية وأراض خصبة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some say ʿAd was the name of their ancestor, so the people were named after their forefather, as with Tamim, Bakr, and Taghlib for their descendants.
rows.anchor: وعاد فيما يقال اسم أبيهم فتسميتهم بعاد من قبيل تسمية القوم باسم أبيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same rationale given for Noah applies: rejecting the one messenger present amounts to rejecting the messengers because they share one call.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم في نظير الآية من قصة نوح وجه عد القوم مكذبين للمرسلين

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some exegetes say these stories stress that the prophets are trustworthy, seek no wage, and command piety and obedience to show their shared mission of true knowledge and conduct leading to reward and away from punishment, despite differences in detailed laws across eras.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن تصدير هذه القصص الخمس بذكر أمانة الرسل وعدم سؤالهم أجرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated ending of all seven stories shows that most peoples turn away from God's signs; God is mighty in requiting deniers and merciful in saving believers, as explained in the surah's purpose.
rows.anchor: ونظيره الكلام في ختم جميع القصص السبع الموردة في السورة بقوله { إن في ذلك لآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rīʿ is elevated ground, āya a marker, and ʿabath an action without a purpose; they built conspicuous structures on peaks and high places for leisure and boasting, without need, so Hud rebuked them.
rows.anchor: الريع هو المرتفع من الأرض والآية العلامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other interpretations of the phrase lack support from its wording and do not fit the context, so al-Tabatabai sets them aside.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكر للآية معان أخر لا دليل عليها من جهة اللفظ ولا ملاءمة للسياق

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some explain maṣāniʿ as strong fortresses, elaborate palaces, or tall buildings; maṣnaʿ is the singular.
rows.anchor: المصانع على ما قيل الحصون المنيعة والقصور المشيدة والأبنية العالية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expectation of immortality explains why they build structures meant to last far beyond human lifetimes; without hoping to live forever, they would not do so.
rows.anchor: في مقام التعليل لما قبله أي تتخذون هذه المصانع بسبب أنكم ترجون الخلود

rows.speaker: مجمع البيان
rows.claim: Majmaʿ al-Bayan defines baṭsh as coercive violence by sword or whip, and jabbār as one who towers over others through great power; the term praises God but blames a human who assumes tyranny.
rows.anchor: قال في المجمع البطش العسف قتلا بالسيف وضربا بالسوط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to fear God and obey follows their excess in both appetite and anger and their departure from servitude; they should abandon indulgence and arrogance.
rows.anchor: ومحصل الآيات الثلاث أنكم مسرفون في جانبي الشهوة والغضب

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib gives the root sense of madd as stretching or drawing out, notes expressions for supplying an army and feeding a person, and says imdad is more common for favorable things while madd often occurs with what is harmful.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب أصل المد الجر، قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command attaches piety to God's description as the one who supplies them, making His provision the reason they owe Him gratitude and should use His gifts without excess or arrogance.
rows.anchor: في معنى تعليق الحكم بالوصف المشعر بالعلية أي اتقوا الله الذي يمدكم بنعمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessings are first summarized as what they know, then itemized as wealth, sons, gardens, and springs.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكر النعم إجمالا بقوله أولا { أمدكم بما تعلمون } ثم فصلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase also argues that they know these blessings come from God's creation and provision alone, so gratitude and worship belong to Him rather than idols.
rows.anchor: هي أنكم تعلمون أن هذه النعم من إمداده تعالى وصنعه لا يشاركه في إيجادها

words: إِنِّىٓ أَخَافُ عَلَيْكُمْ عَذَابَ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear of a great day of punishment explains the call to piety: Hud fears for them if they disbelieve and fail to give thanks; the apparent referent is Judgment Day, though some allow the day of annihilating punishment.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد باليوم العظيم يوم القيامة وإن جوز بعضهم أن يكون المراد به يوم عذاب الاستئصال

words: سَوَآءٌ عَلَيْنَا أَوَعَظْتَ أَمْ لَمْ تَكُن مِّنَ ٱلْوَٰعِظِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their response denies any effect from Hud's words and gives up entirely on belief; the wording exaggerates this by saying he might not even count among admonishers, rather than simply saying he did not admonish.
rows.anchor: نفي لأثر كلامه وإيآس له من إيمانهم بالكلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Replacing “whether you admonished or did not admonish” with “whether you were not among the admonishers” heightens the dismissal by negating even his status as an admonisher.
rows.anchor: فقد كان مقتضى الترديد أن يقال أوعظت أم لم تعظ ففي العدول عنه

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib says khalq and khuluq were originally alike; khalq (fatḥa) came to denote visible forms, while khuluq (ḍamma) denotes inward powers and dispositions, citing the description of the Prophet's great character.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب الخلق والخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term is described with the khāʾ and lām vocalized or with a quiescent lām, and a reading is reported for “this is only the way of the ancients.”
rows.anchor: الخلق بضم الخاء واللام أو سكونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “This” refers to Hud's teaching; they dismiss his monotheistic preaching and admonition as nothing but an old human custom, like calling it tales of the ancients.
rows.anchor: والمعنى ليس ما تلبست به من الدعوة إلى التوحيد والموعظة إلا عادة البشر الأولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabatabai says Lot's preceding argument rests on a demonstrative proof to which the discussion points, also reflected in the parallel wording cited from al-ʿAnkabut.
rows.anchor: وقد ظهر من جميع ما مر أن كلامه عليه السلام مبني على حجة برهانية أشير إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They threaten to expel Lot from their town, as their other statement makes explicit: drive Lot's family out of the town.
rows.anchor: أي المبعدين المنفيين من قريتنا كما نقل عنهم في موضع آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their deed means intercourse with males and abandoning females, as the context indicates; qālī means one who hates.
rows.anchor: إتيان الذكران وترك الإناث. والقالي المبغض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lot answers their threat without addressing it, signaling that he does not fear exile; he despises their deed and wants to escape its inevitable punishment.
rows.anchor: يفيد من المعنى أني لا أخاف الخروج من قريتكم ولا أكترث به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lot's prayer may seek rescue from the sinful act itself, which he witnesses and rejects, or from the punishment that must follow it.
rows.anchor: أي من أصل عملهم الذي يأتون به بمرئى ومسمع منه فهو منزجر منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lot names only himself and his family because no one else in the town believed him; only one house of Muslims was found there.
rows.anchor: وإنما لم يذكر إلا نفسه وأهله إذ لم يكن آمن به من أهل القرية أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ghābir is said to mean those left behind after the others departed; tadmīr means destruction, and the remaining wording is clear.
rows.anchor: الغابر كما قيل الباقي بعد ذهاب من كان معه، والتدمير الإهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rain sent upon them was the stones of sijjīl, as another verse states explicitly.
rows.anchor: وهو السجيل كما قال تعالى وأمطرنا عليهم حجارة من سجيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The concluding claim that this is a sign and that God is mighty and merciful has already been explained in the earlier story endings.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى { إن في ذلك لآية } إلى قوله
